claims.text: For initially solid-solution nanoparticles containing five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios, structural stability from 473 to 1923 K is governed by preservation of the solid-solution phase.
Chemical stability over 473–1923 K is governed by suppression of elemental segregation.
Structural and chemical stability over 473–1923 K is governed by suppression of phase separation.
A stable material will exhibit less than 10% deviation in lattice parameter relative to its value at 298 K throughout 473–1923 K.
A chemically stable material will exhibit less than 10% deviation in chemical composition relative to its composition at 298 K throughout 473–1923 K.
Kinetic limitations may affect phase separation.

contradictions.description: The prediction defines stability as less than 10% deviation, whereas falsification requires more than 20% deviation. Results between 10% and 20%, and potentially exactly 20%, would violate the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
